provenance: The original Phase 6 37-question validation corpus referenced in docs/ENTERPRISE_DELIVERY_PROGRAM.md (M-19, M-20) could not be located in session memory, generated artifacts, repository content, or git history (including deleted files). Only 8 individual questions survived, quoted inline in re-validation tables. This suite is a NEWLY AUTHORED replacement, not a recovery of the original, and is the permanent Enterprise Acceptance Test Suite going forward. Approved as a framework at 45 questions (7 categories), then expanded to its locked v1.0.0 form (98 questions, 26 categories) before freeze, per explicit instruction. All 45 originally-approved ids retain their original id/question/expected_intent unchanged; this expansion only added new ids and added the new expected_outcome/category fields to every entry (additive metadata, not a content change to any existing id).
domain_grounding: CCPP staffing/recruiting vocabulary (client, candidate, placement, job order, student, payroll, invoice, recruiter, enrollment, course, interview) — consistent with the vocabulary already validated end-to-end against the real connected CCPP source in milestones M-1 through M-20.
immutability_policy: Once locked, existing entries (id, question, expected_intent, expected_outcome) are immutable. Changes are made only via additive new versions (v1.1.0, v2.0.0, ...) appended in a new file alongside this one; this file is never edited in place after lock. Every future milestone that touches question classification, semantic resolution, SQL planning, SQL generation, or answering must validate against this exact suite and report pass/fail per category.

schema_notes.expected_intent: The correct target IntentType classification per business logic — the value the resolver should produce once correctly implemented, not necessarily what the current code returns today.
schema_notes.expected_outcome: The correct target pipeline outcome for the question AS WRITTEN, using the controlled vocabulary in expected_outcome_values below. Two different evidentiary standards apply, and each entry's notes field says which one was used: (1) EVIDENCE-BASED — for any question whose exact text was already run against real, live CCPP data and documented in docs/ENTERPRISE_DELIVERY_PROGRAM.md (M-19/M-20 re-validation tables), expected_outcome mirrors that documented, reproduced finding verbatim, including known-wrong/known-defect results. (2) ARCHITECTURAL-TARGET — for every other question, expected_outcome represents the correct outcome assuming an adequately governed/disambiguated instance of the resolved concept, since CCPP's specific 0%-dictionary-approval / sparse-taxonomy data-quality state is a separate, already-tracked gap (W-5, W-8, M-4, M-5), not something this suite exists to re-litigate on every single entry. The dedicated 'Ambiguous Business Concepts' category deliberately uses evidence-based AMBIGUOUS outcomes for CCPP's specific documented ambiguous concept terms.

expected_outcome_values.meaning: Resolves and executes (or answers, for metadata/dictionary/governance intents) producing a correct result.
The pipeline correctly refuses rather than guessing or producing wrong/invalid SQL (semantic-incompatibility guard, out-of-graph reference guard, ungoverned PII, insufficient key confidence, etc.).
Multiple candidate tables/columns tie within the ambiguity margin; correctly surfaced as unresolved with ranked candidates rather than auto-selected.

Target UX outcome: the system should ask the user a clarifying follow-up question. Encodes target state for the not-yet-implemented clarification flow (M-11, status Not Started as of this suite's creation) — today's actual behavior for these ids is AMBIGUOUS structural output, not an actual clarifying question.

The capability needed to answer correctly (trend/period-over-period, ratio/percentage, null-handling aggregation, cross-source query) does not exist yet in the pipeline; a documented, scoped-out gap, not a bug.
The pipeline currently produces an incorrect (silently wrong, not refused) result for this exact question, reproduced and documented in ENTERPRISE_DELIVERY_PROGRAM.md as open residual scope.

changelog.note: Initial lock. 45 originally-approved questions (7 categories) expanded to 98 questions across 26 categories per explicit pre-lock expansion instruction, then locked. See provenance.

categories.name: Counts
categories.description: Questions whose correct answer is an entity/record cardinality (COUNT), not a stored metric.

questions.question: How many active clients are there?
How many candidates do we have?
How many placements were made this quarter?
How many open job orders are there?
How many unique recruiters worked on placements last month?
Total number of invoices this year
How many students are currently enrolled?
questions.notes: EVIDENCE-BASED. Near-paraphrase of M-20's documented 'How many students are enrolled?', reproduced against real CCPP as REFUSED — 'No confident entity-count match for students' (~88 ambiguous candidate tables, no clearing margin). The 'currently' qualifier does not change the underlying term-ambiguity cause.

categories.name: Lists
categories.description: Imperative or bare requests to display a set of business records, with no aggregation language.

categories.name: Aggregations
categories.description: Questions requiring SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX over a stored measure column.

questions.question: Total revenue this year
questions.notes: EVIDENCE-BASED. Exact text reproduced against real CCPP and documented in M-19: pre-M-19 wrongly generated SUM(ADF_YearExpRq.YearsExpValue); post-M-19 correctly blocked by the semantic_compatible guard ('year' implies DATE, resolved concept is AMOUNT).

questions.question: Average time to fill per job order
Students by course
questions.notes: EVIDENCE-BASED. Exact text documented in M-19/M-20: contains no COUNT/SUM trigger language, so extract_query_intent returns aggregation=None; the older _infer_aggregation() column-name-heuristic fallback still silently applies SUM(ADF_ClassPositionAnalytics.TotalStudents) — a wrong aggregation shape. Reproduced, documented, unfixed as of M-20; tracked as open residual scope.

questions.question: Show students enrolled in programs
questions.notes: EVIDENCE-BASED. Same documented M-19/M-20 defect as EBVS-A-07 (SUM(TotalStudents) via the column-name-heuristic fallback, no COUNT/SUM language detected). Reproduced, documented, unfixed as of M-20.

categories.name: Time Intelligence
categories.description: Questions using recency or relative-date phrasing without explicit SQL/analytical vocabulary.

categories.name: Filters
categories.description: Questions filtered by a bare status word (active/inactive/open/closed/pending/cancelled/completed).

questions.question: Pending submissions
questions.notes: Deliberate exception, confirmed 2026-07-13: bare 'pending' is reserved for the REVIEW queue intent to avoid misrouting genuine review-queue questions (e.g. 'pending review', 'pending approval'). 'Pending' status filtering on a business question only reaches SQL_REQUEST when paired with another SQL_REQUEST signal elsewhere in the question, not from the bare status word alone.

categories.name: Relationships
categories.description: Business questions requiring a join across two entities, plus explicit relationship-structure meta-questions (distinct from IntentType.RELATIONSHIP's schema-metadata scope).

questions.question: Which clients have open job orders?
Show candidates linked to active placements
Which students are enrolled in which courses?
How are clients and invoices related?
questions.notes: Meta-question about schema relationship structure, not a request for business records — correctly IntentType.RELATIONSHIP, not SQL_REQUEST.

questions.question: What tables are connected to the placements table?
questions.notes: Same as EBVS-R-05: schema-relationship metadata question, not a business-record request.

questions.question: Show trends in placements over the last 6 months
questions.notes: 'show trend'/'show trends' is an existing REPORT_GENERATION primary keyword (requires the two words adjacent) — routes through the CSV/dataset report pipeline, a separate mechanism from live SQL. Correctly out of the live-SQL pipeline, not a gap. CORRECTION 2026-07-13: original wording ('Show placement trends...') did not have 'show' and 'trend(s)' adjacent and so never matched; caught during the first post-implementation validation pass, before this suite was used for real, and reworded here rather than left wrong under a false 'locked' label.
